title: Executable Images and OS Loading
description: Follow a program from an executable image to its first instruction: the kernel's mapping, the auxiliary vector, the initial stack and the addresses you are handed.
author: Underlayer
completion_criteria: Read all 6 concepts, reproduce the 41 measured checks in courses/img/assets/samples/crosscheck.py, and run courses/img/assets/samples/stackwalk.py

concepts.title: The Auxiliary Vector
concepts.description: The third array on the initial stack, the one no C library function will give you.

concepts.title: Reading the Initial Stack by Hand
concepts.description: argc, argv, envp, auxv as raw bytes, and the off-by-one that segfaults.

concepts.title: What Each Entry Is For
concepts.description: The three that matter, the arithmetic that ties them to the file, and the pointer-versus-size trap.

concepts.title: The vDSO: An ELF File With No File
concepts.description: A shared library the kernel synthesises, maps into every process, and backs with nothing.

concepts.title: Where the Kernel Put Everything
concepts.description: The process map, the 64 KB floor, and why a hint is not a request.

concepts.title: Rebuilding the Image Reader
concepts.description: Read the raw stack, decode it with no libc, and check every value against the file and against procfs.

exercise_decls.question: Complete this sentence from the lesson: Five courses into this chain you can read a relocation record, a linker script, a ______ entry, and the loader’s own symbol bindings. Every one of those facts lives in a file. Now ask the question none of them could answer: when the kernel runs that file, how does the program find out where it landed?

Every one of those facts lives in a file. Now ask the question none of them could answer: when the kernel runs that file, how does the program find out where it landed?

exercise_decls.question: Complete this sentence from the lesson: Trap one: ______ inside main is not the stack pointer the kernel set. Trap two: the auxv is not the array after envp — it is the array after the NULL that ends envp, and the difference is one word.
exercise_decls.explanation: The lesson states: Trap one: %rsp inside main is not the stack pointer the kernel set. Trap two: the auxv is not the array after envp — it is the array after the NULL that ends envp, and the difference is one word.

exercise_decls.question: Complete this sentence from the lesson: Every dynamic process on Linux maps a shared library that has no file on disk. It appears in ______ under the name [vdso] — square brackets, which is the kernel’s way of saying there is no path here. It has an address, given to the process in the auxv as AT_SYSINFO_EHDR. And it has, if you read it, a perfectly ordinary ELF header.
